case_brief.subject: UGC Fee Refund Policy
case_brief.what_it_is: The UGC Fee Refund Policy mandates that Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) must refund fees to students who withdraw their admission. It applies to all HEIs, including those established under Central or State Acts, deemed universities, and affiliated institutions.
case_brief.entitlement: Students are entitled to a refund of fees upon withdrawal of admission, with the specific amount determined by the date of withdrawal relative to the formally notified last date of admission. Institutions are required to process these refunds, though they may deduct a processing fee of not more than ₹1,000 in specific scenarios.
conditions: For admissions before 31 October 2024, a full refund is provided for cancellations made up to 30 September 2024.
For admissions before 31 October 2024, a refund with a maximum deduction of ₹1,000 as a processing fee is provided for cancellations made between 1 October 2024 and 31 October 2024.
For admissions after 31 October 2024, a 100% refund is provided if the withdrawal notice is received 15 days or more before the formally notified last date of admission.
For admissions after 31 October 2024, a 90% refund is provided if the withdrawal notice is received less than 15 days before the formally notified last date of admission.
For admissions after 31 October 2024, an 80% refund is provided if the withdrawal notice is received 15 days or less after the formally notified last date of admission.
For admissions after 31 October 2024, a 50% refund is provided if the withdrawal notice is received 30 days or less, but more than 15 days after the formally notified last date of admission.
For admissions after 31 October 2024, a 0% refund is provided if the withdrawal notice is received more than 30 days after the formally notified last date of admission.
common_failure_reasons: HEIs violating the policy by refusing to refund fees
Lack of awareness of the policy by students or parents

case_brief.subject: UGC Fee Refund Policy
case_brief.what_it_is: The UGC Fee Refund Policy mandates that Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) must refund fees to students who withdraw their admission. It applies to all HEIs, including those established under Central or State Acts, deemed universities, and affiliated institutions.
case_brief.entitlement: Students are entitled to a refund of fees upon withdrawal of admission, with the specific amount determined by the date of withdrawal relative to the formally notified last date of admission. Institutions are required to process these refunds, though they may deduct a processing fee of not more than ₹1,000 in specific scenarios.
case_brief.official_grievance_channel: University Grants Commission (UGC) under the Redressal of Grievances of Students Regulations, 2023
